exposure: Mechanical cervical dilatation during elective cesarean section
mechanical cervical dilatation during elective cesarean section
cohort: 422 pregnant women with a singleton fetus at term ≥37 weeks of gestation scheduled for elective cesarean section at a tertiary university hospital
finding: Cervical dilatation during elective cesarean section was associated with thicker scars, a lower incidence of scar defects, and a lower incidence of febrile morbidity.
mod_finding: Cervical dilatation during elective cesarean section was associated with thicker scars, a lower incidence of scar defects, and a lower incidence of febrile morbidity.
